text:
marta: Heads up — we saw a 3x latency spike on gpu-rtus-4 between 09:12 and 09:18 UTC. Dashboards show throughput collapse on that host but traces are sparse for the same window. Any initial thoughts?

alex: saw the same. Quick glance: kernel selection flipped to fallback_mmap for many inflight requests around 09:12.

jen: my lightweight profiler from 08:55 shows heavy KV cache churn on that node — evictions spiking. Could be a noisy tenant triggering memory pressure.

sre-oncall: incident-bot created INC-2026-032 and paged oncall.

marta: linking graphs: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/rt-kv/gpu-rtus-4?panelId=7 — eviction & p50 panels.

alex: logs contain sampler annotations like `span_missing=true sample_rate=0.05`. We rolled trace-sampling changes yesterday.

jen: posted the sampling config we shipped: ```
trace_sampling:
  default_rate: 0.01
  host_overrides:
    gpu-rtus-4: 0.0
```

marta: oh — we set gpu-rtus-4 to 0 to cut trace volume from a noisy host. That likely hid the trace sequences needed to connect kernel_selector -> eviction events. Can we safely increase sampling for a short window?

alex: agreed. But we need a quick correlation method without full traces. You can query metrics API with 1s resolution: `/api/rt/metrics?hosts=gpu-rtus-4&series=kernel_selector,kv_evictions,latency_p50` — I ran it and saw: kernel_selector flips from fast_cuda -> fallback_mmap at 09:12:23, kv_evictions spike at 09:12:20, p50 jumps at 09:12:24.

jen: that timeline matches eviction -> kernel fallback -> latency jump. Noisy tenant looks like alpha-sms based on logs `tenant_id=alpha-sms` and burst_rate spikes.

sre-oncall: can we throttle or isolate alpha-sms quickly? Any mitigation steps?

marta: options: 1) move alpha-sms to different pool (needs infra change), 2) apply per-tenant burst quota, 3) temporarily throttle their requests at the rate-limiter. Which is fastest?

alex: I applied a temporary sampler rollback and bumped trace sampling for gpu-rtus-4 to 0.25 to capture traces while we debug. Pushed change at 09:30 UTC. Please monitor storage.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-032 updated: sampling override applied by alex at 09:30 UTC.

jen: quick correlation table I generated: `tenant,burst_multiplier,eviction_delta,kernel_fallbacks` -> `alpha-sms,1.8x,+6x,+1200`. CSV pasted to #eng-runtime.

marta: good catch. Can eng-runtime schedule a follow-up to add a host-level alert when eviction_rate > 5x baseline AND kernel_selector != fast_cuda? That would help detect early memory-pressure-induced fallbacks.

alex: +1. Also we should avoid setting host trace sampling to 0 for production nodes that we rely on for debugability. Maybe prefer sampling reduction for specific tenants rather than host-level blackholing.

jen: noted. I'll open a PR to change policy to tenant-level sampling overrides and add a temporary dashboard tile to track host-sampled-span-rate so we don't accidentally blind ourselves.

marta: thanks everyone. For now mitigation path: throttle alpha-sms bursts + revert host sampling override. Follow-up meeting in eng-runtime at 11:00. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: current status: alpha-sms throttled, sampling bumped, latency trending down but still above baseline. Will update incident with a postmortem link when we have one.
